item.title: French government says 320,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday
item.description: Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates ...
item.dc:creator: AP
item.content:encoded: The French government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide Saturday in demonstrations focused on high living costs, fewer than in previous demonstrations.Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates. Organisers' turnout estimates are much higher.The Interior Ministry told reporters that of the 320,000 protesting Saturday, 70,000 people are estimated to have turned out for the main protest in Paris, which police moved outside the city centre to reduce the risk of unrest around government buildings and tourist sites after a last-minute court battle.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty

Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty Besides, Sebi has imposed monetary penalties totalling Rs 88 lakh on the company and other individuals for various violations of securities market regulations

SEBI (File Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 31 2026 | 10:17 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Markets regulator Sebi has barred EKI Energy Services Ltd and its Managing Director Manish Kumar Dabkara from the securities market for two months and 12 months, respectively, for misrepresenting financial statements of the carbon credits trading firm and diverting funds. Also, the regulator has restrained the company's former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Mohit Kumar Agarwal from the securities market for eight months, while whole-time directors Naveen Sharma and Sonali Sheikh have been prohibited for five months and one month, respectively. Besides, Sebi has imposed monetary penalties totalling ₹88 lakh on the company and other individuals for various violations of securities market regulations.

Further, the markets regulator directed Dabkara to take immediate steps to recoup the amount diverted from EKI Energy Services. In its 94-page final order, Sebi noted that EKI had prematurely recognised revenue aggregating ₹197.04 crore during the first three quarters of FY23, thereby misrepresenting its financial performance to investors. The regulator observed that "EKI's publication and continued disclosure of prematurely recognised revenue of ₹197.04 crore constituted reckless financial misrepresentation connected with investor decisions concerning its listed shares". Also, the regulator found that EKI had overstated expenses by ₹26.34 crore during FY22 and FY23, resulting in an understatement of its profits. "The company diverted ₹26.34 crore by overstating expenses during 2021-22 and 2022-23," the order said.

The regulator noted that EKI had "booked fictitious expenses against services not rendered", adding that payments made against such expenses "consequently constituted diversion of EKI's funds". Also, Sebi noted that Dabkara was responsible for the continued disclosure of misstated financial information and failure to ensure proper monitoring of the company's financial reporting systems. Also, the regulator held Sharma, Sheikh, and Agarwal liable for regulatory violations. Sebi imposed a penalty of ₹12 lakh on EKI Energy Services, ₹28 lakh on Dabkara, ₹13 lakh on Sharma, ₹6 lakh on Sheikh and ₹19 lakh on Agarwal. Sebi also imposed monetary penalties on independent directors Ritesh Gupta and Burhanuddin Ali Husain Maksi Wala, besides former compliance officer Itisha Sahu. It levied a fine of ₹2 lakh on Sahu and ₹4 lakh each on Gupta and Burhanuddin Ali Husain Maksi Wala.

The entities have been directed to pay the penalties within 45 days.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / US Secretary of State Rubio hosts Quad meet, wraps up G20 gathering

US Secretary of State Rubio hosts Quad meet, wraps up G20 gathering Rubio hosted a final plenary session with foreign ministers from the Group of 20 major economies during a two-day summit in Atlanta

In this image released on Oct. 31, 2026, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and other dignitaries during the G20 Ministerial Summit, in Atlanta, United States (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 31 2026 | 9:51 PM IST

US ??Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted a meeting with the foreign ministers of Australia, India and Japan on Saturday, their third meeting this year, as plans take shape for a summit of the leaders of the four countries in Manila next month.   The leaders' summit, expected to occur during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) conference in the Philippine capital on November 15-18, would be the first since 2024, and the first for US President Donald Trump.   The first formal leaders' summits of the four countries known as the Quad did not begin until President Joe Biden took office in 2021. Trump was scheduled to attend a Quad summit in India in late 2025, but canceled the visit due to trade frictions and tariff disputes with New Delhi.

After the Quad ministers' meeting, Rubio hosted a final plenary session with foreign ministers from the Group of 20 major economies during a two-day summit in Atlanta, where the participation of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov highlighted deep rifts among G20 members.   Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand told Reuters in an interview that she would not have chosen to invite Lavrov, but she used the occasion to confront him directly about Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.   Also Read

Military solutions not working, give diplomacy a chance: Jaishankar at G20

Jaishankar slams global energy disruptions through sanctions, chokepoints

Nvidia chief Jensen Huang reportedly targeted in Chinese spy plot

Refining the crude argument premium

Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes despite renewed US push for peace

"I stared him in the eye and called out Russia's further illegal invasion of Ukraine, the stealing of Ukrainian children, the targeting of Ukrainian ships in the Black Sea, all of which are reprehensible, all of which are contrary to international law and international humanitarian law," Anand said, citing her remarks during a closed-door plenary ??session on Friday.

Lavrov on Friday told reporters that Moscow's position on the Ukraine conflict was unchanged, and Russia could not accept Ukraine as a "military threat to the lawful security interests of the Russian Federation," according to Russian news agencies.   Rubio, speaking at a reception at the Georgia Aquarium on Friday evening, repeated his call for G20 members to cooperate where possible given today's complex economic and geopolitical challenges, including many with serious global consequences. "Because we all face these challenges, we must all work together to address them," he said.   "The future of our nations depends on our willingness to understand that while our interests may not always align, we should always seek to work together to advance them when and where they do align."

Rubio, who will hold a press conference after the meetings conclude on Saturday, said he hoped the G20 foreign ministers could lay the groundwork for a successful leaders' summit on December 14-15 at Trump's Doral golf resort near Miami.

item.title: Jio Platforms Q2 profit rises 13.7% to ₹8,387 crore, revenue up 11.4%
item.description: Jio Platforms reported a 13.7% rise in Q2FY27 net profit to ₹8,389 crore, marking its first quarterly results since the telecom and digital major's record $3.2 billion stock market debut.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / Quarterly Results / Jio Platforms Q2 profit rises 13.7% to ₹8,387 crore, revenue up 11.4%

Jio Platforms Q2 profit rises 13.7% to ₹8,387 crore, revenue up 11.4% JPL IPO broke records across all investor categories; a milestone for the next growth phase: MD Akash Ambani

The company listed on the BSE on October 28, raising Rs 30,188 crore in what was termed India's largest public offering

Gulveen Aulakh New Delhi 6 min read Last Updated : Oct 30 2026 | 11:38 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL), the parent company of India’s largest telecom-services provider Reliance Jio, on Friday reported a net profit of ₹8,389 crore for July-September 2026-27 in its first earnings report after its blockbuster market listing earlier this week.     Net profit was up 13.7 per cent from ₹7,379 crore in the same period last financial year.   Revenues rose 11.4 per cent to ₹40,475 crore from ₹36,332 crore the same quarter last year.   In the previous quarter, profits were ₹7,764 crore and revenues ₹39,173 crore. The company raised ₹30,188 crore in what is India’s largest initial public offering. Also Read

“We were raising ₹30,000 crore-odd, and we saw demand of over ₹7.5 trillion. We saw every investor category broken, starting from QIB (qualified institutional buyers) to small HNI (high net worth), big HNI, retail, and all the various shareholders, employees, all of the categories were broken,” said Akash Ambani, managing director, JPL, at the analyst call following the results.

The top executive at India’s second-largest company by market capitalisation said that JPL’s IPO numbers came at a time when the Indian markets had seen outflows of more than ₹48,000 crore, led by foreign portfolio investors.   “In a market situation like that, (we are) very proud that the people (are) realising (what) business we’ve built ... we put in extremely hard work over the last 10 years to build this business, and we’ll continue to do so,” Ambani noted, adding, the IPO was a new milestone, and that the company would move on from here.   “We believe that you know the value that we can create over the next decade or so is even more than what we have done in our first decade, and we’ll continue to aspire to that perspective,” he said.

Quarterly earnings before interest tax, depreciation and amortisation climbed 16.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹21,879 crore. The 250-basis point rise in margins was driven by revenue growth and operating leverage.   Jio reported average revenue per user (Arpu), a monthly metric of profitability of a telecom services provider, at ₹218.8, marginally up from ₹215.6 in Q1FY27. However, year-on-year, Arpu was up 3.5 per cent, from ₹211.4, on the back of promotional schemes for fixed broadband customers and increased usage.   “We warmly welcome our new shareholders to the Jio Platforms family as we enter a new era as a listed company. This quarter’s results continue to reflect the strength of our 5G network, and the growing reach of our broadband and digital services,” Ambani said in a statement to the exchanges.

The company said in its statement to the stock exchanges that ₹27,500 crore from the net proceeds from the IPO has been used to prepay, in full or in part, the principal amount outstanding of the external commercial borrowing of Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, a material subsidiary of JPL, and the balance amount would be for general corporate purposes. JPL’s net debt reduced by 78.6 per cent to ₹8,822 crore from ₹41,161 crore in Q2FY26. Debt reduced quarter-on-quarter by 7.5 per cent from ₹9,539 crore in Q1FY27.   Finance costs rose 40.3 per cent to ₹3,009 crore, up from ₹2,145 crore in Q2FY26.

Reliance Jio ended September 2026 with 542.4 million users, including 300 million 5G subscribers. The carrier added 9.1 million subscribers during the quarter.

Jio’s 5G data traffic in the fourth quarter reached 71.3 billion gigabytes, while total voice traffic rose 1.3 per cent to 1.52 trillion minutes. It added 66 million 5G customers over the last 12 months, and 15 million over the past quarter. Customer engagement also remains robust with data consumption at 44.2 GB per month, higher than 38.7 GB per month in the same period last year.   Fixed broadband subscribers as of September 2026 stood at 30 million with about 7.3 million additions over the last 12 months.

Jio AirFiber had over 15.1 million subscribers, driving more than 75 per cent of the fixed broadband additions during the last 12 months, the company said. “Ahead of the curve investment on next generation technologies has been the foundation of Jio’s success over the past decade. We would continue to build our capabilities across satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and AI embedded in our core voice and data services as we create lasting value for all our stakeholders,” Ambani added. He elaborated the company’s strategy, noting that it was unlike a traditional telecom services provider owing largely to its proprietary technology with integrated 4G, 5G stack, unlicensed broadband radio (UBR) and now fixed wireless becoming 50 per cent of its base.

He added that Jio would double down on offers to the enterprise because it would be a major growth opportunity, with India having 350,000 lease lines.    On expanding internationally, Ambani said that the company would be “very selective” about the markets that it would go to.   “We will not be selling our proprietary stacks as a hardware commission … What we imagine the business model here to be is to be actually managed service partner with our customers. It’s not going to be a heavy capex rollout. You won’t see us going and putting up towers and fiber and infrastructure only. But this is something that we think that will be enabled because of the only proprietary stack that we have," he added.

Stating the company’s competitive advantage — owing to full-stack technology across seven layers, deep engineering and proprietary IP contribution — Ambani said Jio had multiple growth engines across mobility, home, enterprise, and international.   “We are the ones that have a clear path of growth and profitability improving with a very strong balance sheet, even before the IPO proceeds come to us,” he added.      ALSO READ:  RIL's O2C Ebitda jumps 68% on higher fuel cracks and chemical margins
